newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania sold off 800 firms in four months - premier. [corrected 09:22 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Romania sold off 800 firms in four months - premier. [corrected 09:22 gmt]

text.p: (Corrects number of privatised firms in headline and first paragraph to 800 from 400)
Romania's Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Tuesday the State Ownership Fund (FPS), the main stockholder of the bulk Romanian state companies, had privatised 800 firms in the past four months.

"This represents about 25 percent of companies sold during 1993 to 1996," Ciorbea told parliament in a report on progress in the reform programme launched soon after the election last November of his centrist government.
Ciorbea's address was intended to secure parliamentary support for the tough reforms, including large budget cuts, reductions in subsidies, faster privatisation and liberalisation of markets.
The leftist opposition has submitted a no confidence motion to the assembly, to be debated later this week.
Ciorbea said only 3,100 companies from over 6,000 state-owned companies were privatised at end-1996.
"Over the past 10 weeks we have privatised some 53 companies per week," Ciorbea said.

Analysts say privatisation and restructuring of communist-era industries were keys to the success of fast-track reforms after seven years of sluggish progress under the cabinet's ex-communist predecessor.
Earlier this year, in order to speed up privatisation Ciorbea's cabinet put the FPS under government control. The FPS was previously responsible solely to parliament.

Slow market reforms under the former lefist administration have kept foreign investors away from Romania. Foreign investments in the Balkan country were a mere $2.3 billion in seven years since Romania ended communist rule, far behind its east European neighbours.
